critical_code_review_comments: api/settings.py: /admin/settings/visuals GET guarded by CMS_READ, PUT by CMS_WRITE — matches RBAC matrix (SUPER_ADMIN via ALL_PERMISSIONS + CONTENT_MANAGER; CUSTOMER_SERVICE has CMS_READ only). Correctly separates permission from role.
PUT visuals uses body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) so partial updates are supported and no field is nulled inadvertently.
Audit log written with entity_type='cms_visuals'; before/after snapshots limited to non-secret visual fields.
Public /api/settings/public exposes only visual + WhatsApp fields; no _id key, no PII, no secret exposure.

NOTE (informational, not a bug): rbac.py grants ADMINISTRATOR only CMS_READ (not CMS_WRITE). The review request mentioned 'ADMINISTRATOR PUT=200'; this is technically 403 by matrix. Because SUPER_ADMIN has ALL_PERMISSIONS anyway, this does not impact tested credentials. If product wants ADMINISTRATOR to also write CMS visuals, add Permission.CMS_WRITE to the ADMINISTRATOR frozenset in auth/rbac.py.
Login flow redirects to /admin/legalitas (default post-login route) rather than /admin/dashboard. Not a spec violation; noting for awareness.
